title: Get Slice From List
description: Extract sub-lists using Get Slice From List for range-based data extraction.

story.setup: MENTOR-9: "Sensor logs contain 100 readings, but we only need the last 10 for analysis. Use Get Slice From List to extract specific ranges without modifying the original data."
story.context: Slicing extracts portions of lists—first N items, last N items, or specific ranges. Essential for pagination, sampling, and windowed analysis.
story.success: MENTOR-9: "Great! You extracted the first 3 items, last 3 items, and a middle range. Slicing is perfect for working with large datasets without loading everything."

instructions: Create *** Settings *** section with Library    Collections
hints: Get Slice From List syntax: start_index    end_index
Start index is inclusive, end index is exclusive
Omit end_index to slice to end: Get Slice From List    ${list}    5
solution:
*** Settings ***
Library    Collections

*** Test Cases ***
Sensor Reading Analysis
    @{readings}=    Create List    10    15    20    25    30    35    40    45    50
    Log    All readings: ${readings}
    ${first_three}=    Get Slice From List    ${readings}    0    3
    Log    First 3: ${first_three}
    ${last_three}=    Get Slice From List    ${readings}    -3
    Log    Last 3: ${last_three}
    ${middle}=    Get Slice From List    ${readings}    3    6
    Log    Middle range: ${middle}
    Should Be Equal    ${first_three}[0]    10
    Should Be Equal    ${last_three}[-1]    50

theory.title: Exercise 4.1.4: List Slicing
theory.content:
MENTOR-9: "You don't always need the entire list. First 10 results for pagination. Last 5 errors for recent issues. Middle section for sampling. Slicing extracts exactly what you need."

Get Slice From List

Extract sub-lists without modifying original:

@{items}=    Create List    A    B    C    D    E    F

# First 3 items
${first}=    Get Slice From List    ${items}    0    3
# Returns: [A, B, C]

# Last 2 items
${last}=    Get Slice From List    ${items}    -2
# Returns: [E, F]

# Middle items (index 2 to 4)
${mid}=    Get Slice From List    ${items}    2    5
# Returns: [C, D, E]

Slicing Rules:

  • Start index: inclusive (0-based)
  • End index: exclusive (item at end_index NOT included)
  • Negative index: counts from end (-1 = last item)
  • Omit end: slices to list end
  • Original list unchanged

Example: Pagination

*** Settings ***
Library    Collections

*** Test Cases ***
Paginate Results
    @{results}=    Create List    ${RANGE(1, 101)}  # 1-100
    ${page_size}=    Set Variable    10
    ${page_1}=    Get Slice From List    ${results}    0    10
    ${page_2}=    Get Slice From List    ${results}    10    20
    Log    Page 1: ${page_1}
    Log    Page 2: ${page_2}

⚠️ Slicing Tips

  • Returns new list (doesn't modify original)
  • Start=0, End=3 returns 3 items (0, 1, 2)
  • Use negative index for "last N items"
  • Great for: pagination, sampling, windowing
  • Combine with FOR loops for batch processing
